definitions.explanation: Having no equal; so strong or skilled that no one compares. A literary word in set phrases such as {天下無双|てんかむそう}, it has become common in casual speech for someone dominating effortlessly, a use that spread from the video game series of that name.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天下無双|てんかむそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{剣士|けんし}→剣士：11912_kenshi⟧だ。
examples.english: He is a swordsman without equal under heaven.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{無双|むそう}だった。
examples.english: Today's match was a one-woman show; nobody could stop her.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{国士無双|こくしむそう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれた→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦{武将|ぶしょう}→武将：13222_bushou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{勝|か}てなかった→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧。
examples.english: Even the general once called the greatest warrior in the land could not beat old age.

notes:
From ⟦{無|む}→無：17750_mu⟧ (no, none) + {双|そう} (pair, equal): literally 'having no match'.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {天下無双|てんかむそう}: unrivaled in the whole world
- {国士無双|こくしむそう}: the greatest person in the country; also a hand in mahjong
- {無双|むそう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: (slang) to dominate, to beat everyone single-handedly

REGISTER:
The set phrases are literary and appear in historical fiction. The slang use ({無双|むそう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧, ～{無双|むそう}) is casual and common among young people and in online writing.

WATCH OUT:
⟦{夢想|むそう}→夢想：21442_musou⟧ (daydream, fantasy) has the same reading.
